title: CloudTrail Log File Delivery Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.30 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.30 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="DeleteTrail" OR eventName="PutBucketPolicy" requestParameters.name=*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.30_cloudtrail_log_file_deli_30"
| sort -_time
description: Failed CloudTrail delivery means audit gaps. Attackers may target trail deletion or S3 permissions to hide activity.
value: Detecting cloudtrail log file delivery failures early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable CloudTrail log file validation. Monitor for DeleteTrail, PutBucketPolicy on the trail bucket, or S3 access denied to trail bucket. Use AWS Config or custom Lambda to validate delivery and alert on gaps.
visualization: Events list (critical), Table (trail, bucket, event), Timeline.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where match(All_Changes.action, "(?i)DeleteTrail|StopLogging|UpdateTrail|PutBucketPolicy|PutEventSelectors") OR match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)cloudtrail|trail")
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Intentional trail or bucket hardening in the same change ticket; always confirm a matching ticket before paging.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CloudTrail log file validation. Monitor for DeleteTrail, PutBucketPolicy on the trail bucket, or S3 access denied to trail bucket. Use AWS Config or custom Lambda to validate delivery and alert on gaps.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="DeleteTrail" OR eventName="PutBucketPolicy" requestParameters.name=*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.30_cloudtrail_log_file_deli_30"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect cloudtrail log file delivery failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_30_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Events list (critical), Table (trail, bucket, event), Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloudtrail log file delivery failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
